Safari & Eco-Tourism

The forests, rivers and reservoirs of Bhadradri Kothagudem District offer scope for nature-friendly tourism. Visitors are requested to follow Forest Department rules and enjoy nature while protecting it.

Book a visit

Visitor guidance

  • Visit only in permitted areas and during approved timings.
  • Follow the instructions of forest staff and guides at all times.
  • Carry a valid photo ID and any required permit.
  • Check timings and entry rules with the Forest Department before travelling.

Responsible tourism

  • Do not litter. Carry your waste back and avoid single-use plastic.
  • Do not feed, touch or disturb wild animals.
  • Keep noise low and avoid loud music.
  • Do not light fires or smoke inside forest areas.
  • Do not pluck plants or collect forest produce.

Activities

Safari, nature walks and bird watching are the kinds of activities offered at approved sites. The activities available at each place will be listed here.

Wildlife

Kothagudem is part of Bhadradri Kothagudem district in Telangana, a region known for its extensive forest areas and rich natural biodiversity. The forests around Kothagudem, Palvancha, Manuguru, Yellandu and Bhadrachalam provide habitats for a variety of wild animals, birds, reptiles and other organisms.

Kinnerasani Wildlife Sanctuary

One of the district’s important wildlife destinations is Kinnerasani Wildlife Sanctuary, which protects forest habitats and supports a variety of wildlife. The surrounding forests are also important for maintaining ecological balance, protecting watersheds and conserving native plant and animal species.

1. Wild Animals

LeopardSpotted deerIndian gaurSambar deerSloth bearWild boar

The forests of Kothagudem support a variety of wild animals and provide important natural habitats for wildlife. The forest areas around Kinnerasani Wildlife Sanctuary are known for species such as leopards, spotted deer, Indian gaur, sambar deer, sloth bears and wild boars.

These animals play an important role in maintaining the ecological balance of the forest. Herbivores such as deer feed on grasses, leaves and other plants, while carnivores such as leopards help regulate prey populations. Protecting these animals and their habitats is essential for preserving the region’s biodiversity and maintaining a healthy forest ecosystem.

2. Birds

Indian peafowlJunglefowlIndian roller (state bird)QuailsPartridgesAsian paradise flycatcher

Kothagudem’s forests, trees, rivers and reservoir surroundings provide suitable habitats for many types of birds. Jungle birds associated with the Kinnerasani region include Indian peafowl, junglefowl, the Indian roller (Telangana’s state bird), quails, partridges and the Asian paradise flycatcher.

These birds help the environment by controlling insect populations, dispersing seeds and supporting the natural food chain. Some birds live mainly in forest areas, while others prefer wetlands and water bodies where they find food and shelter. Protecting trees, water sources and natural habitats helps conserve bird diversity and ensures that future generations can continue to enjoy the region’s rich wildlife.

About the District

Bhadradri Kothagudem is the easternmost and the largest district of Telangana, known for its forests, the Godavari river, coal mining and the sacred town of Bhadrachalam. Kothagudem is the district headquarters.

KothagudemHeadquarters
4.76 lakh acresForest cover in the district (as reported; to be verified)
21Forest ranges in the district
6Forest divisions: Kothagudem, Bhadrachalam, Manuguru, Paloncha, Kinnerasani, Yellandu

Geography and resources

Bhadradri Kothagudem lies in the east of Telangana and borders Chhattisgarh to the north and north-east. Much of the district is drained by the Godavari river. It has rich forests, including the Kinnerasani Wildlife Sanctuary, and coal is its major mineral resource.

People and heritage

A large share of residents are tribal communities, with Scheduled Tribes making up over a third of the population. Bhadrachalam, on the bank of the Godavari, is a major pilgrimage town known for the Sri Sita Ramachandra Swamy temple, and the district is named after the Bhadradri hill there.

Forests and wildlife

The district’s forests are managed through six forest divisions. See the Maps section for division, range and beat boundaries.
